raw_response:
I’m already old now, and I don’t like making big changes. What worked on my land before, I mostly keep doing. Cotton is still my main crop, because in our area many people with this kind of land still rely on it, but I also keep some wheat and maize on part of the land so the family has steadier income and I’m not betting everything on one crop. Money is not loose at home, and some people work outside, so I can’t watch the field every day like before. I will not chase the highest yield. I want a stable harvest and not spend too much cash at one time. For cotton, I’ll put more care because that is the crop I count on. For wheat and maize, I’ll do them the usual local way, not too little input, not too fancy either. If water is tight or costs go up, I’ll first protect cotton and wheat, and maize I can be a bit more flexible if summer rain is decent.

decision.reasoning_summary: This year I still put most of my 20 mu into cotton, 12 mu, because that is my main way of farming and I know this crop better. But I keep 8 mu in wheat-maize rotation too, so if one crop price is bad or the weather is not good, I still have something. I do not dare cut fertilizer too much, because if the crop turns weak later it is hard to make up. At the same time, I cannot spend carelessly, so I use moderate rates, mostly the same as what has worked before in our village. Since some family members work outside, I keep the plan simple and follow the local timing.
